close_reason: Added the 5 missing RFC 8984 §4.4.6 Participant fields (scheduleForceSend: Option<bool>, sentBy: Option<String>, progress: Option<String>, progressUpdated: Option<UTCDate>, percentComplete: Option<u8>) with verbatim spec-text rustdoc per field. Non-breaking because Participant is #[non_exhaustive]. Added a round-trip test (participant_new_rfc8984_fields_round_trip) using a hand-built JSON oracle whose shape comes from the RFC 8984 §4.4.6 spec text — independent oracle, not the code under test. cargo test + cargo clippy -D warnings clean; downstream jmap-calendars-types tests still pass.
description:
RFC 8984 §4.4.6 defines Participant with the following fields that the current Rust struct does not type:

- scheduleForceSend: Boolean (optional, default false) — client-set flag requesting server to send a scheduling message even when not normal. Spec note: 'The property MUST NOT be stored in the JSCalendar object on the server or appear in a scheduling message' — but it still appears in client-to-server requests and a typed binding is needed for clients.
- sentBy: String (optional) — email in the From header of the last iMIP update for this participant. Validity: addr-spec.
- progress: String (optional; Task-only) — per-participant Task progress.
- progressUpdated: UTCDateTime (optional; Task-only) — timestamp progress was last set.
- percentComplete: UnsignedInt 0–100 (optional; Task-only) — per-participant Task completion.

Trigger: any consumer (jmap-calendars-types today, jmap-tasks-types tomorrow per bd:JMAP-yfpq) deserializing a Participant with any of these fields gets them rolled into Participant.extra rather than typed-field access.

Bad behavior: serde round-trip is preserved by extras (workspace policy), but typed code paths cannot read or write these fields. The Task-only trio is especially load-bearing for the upcoming jmap-tasks-types consumer — Tasks per-participant progress is a first-class RFC concept.

Severity: this is an incomplete-binding bug, not a wire bug. Extras catches the data so deployments do not silently drop information, but consumers cannot reach it through Rust types. Since Participant is #[non_exhaustive] the fix is non-breaking.

Fix: add the five fields with appropriate Option<T> types (Option<bool>, Option<String>, Option<String>, Option<UTCDate>, Option<u8>). Add round-trip tests for each.
title: Participant missing 5 RFC 8984 §4.4.6 typed fields (scheduleForceSend, sentBy, progress, progressUpdated, percentComplete)
